item.title: Who was the Most Valuable and Needed NBA Player in the 25-26 season?
item.dc:creator: JR Rhodes-Winfrey
item.description:
The NBA has been a highly competitive atmosphere, as many new and younger players have put the veterans on notice. In the days of old, we could see LeBron James, Kevin Durant, and James Harden competing for the Most Valuable Player title; however, they have fallen out of their former glory. Coming into the previous season, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander won the title, scoring 31.1 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 6.6 assists per game; however, was this MVP deserved? Other big names from different teams, such as Victor Wembanyama for the San Antonio Spurs, Donovan Mitchell for the Cleveland Cavaliers, or Tyrese Maxey for the Philadelphia 76ers, are pushing the envelope to see who can take the Most Valuable trophy, which led to the question of “Who really was the Most Valuable Player?

Code 
library(tidyverse)
library(hoopR)
library(ggrepel)
library(gt)

impact <- load_nba_player_impact(
  seasons = c(2025,2026)
) |> 
  mutate(playerseason = paste(player_name, season))

playerimpact <- impact |>
  filter(min >= 1300 & gp >= 65 & bpm >= 5 & war >= 10 & playerseason > 2025) |> 
  arrange(desc(bpm))

ggplot() + 
  geom_point(data=playerimpact, aes(x=min, y=bpm, color = playerseason)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
  "darkgreen", #Giannis Antetokounmpo
  "red",  #Kawhi Leonard
  "purple",  #Nikola Jokić 2025
  "gold", #Nikola Jokić 
   "pink",  #Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 2025
  "orange",  #Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
  "royalblue",  #Stephen Curry
   "navy"  #Tyrese Maxey
  ) )+
    annotate("rect", fill = "red", alpha = 0.1, 
        xmin = 2550, xmax = Inf,
        ymin = 10, ymax = Inf) +
  geom_text(aes(x=2500, y=10, label="Most Valuable Players"), size=3) +
  labs(
    x="NBA Top Contenders", 
    y="Wins Above Replacement", 
    title="Who in the NBA were the Most Irreplaceable Players?", 
    subtitle="Jokic and Shai were the most key players for their teams for their past seasons.", 
    caption="Source: JR Rhodes-Winfrey"
    ) +
  theme_minimal()  +  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
  )

Looking at this graph, we see our first glimpses of our main cast for this investigation. You see previous title holders such as one-time winner Giannis Antetokounmpo, two-time winner Stephen Curry, two-time and reigning two-time Most Valuable Player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, three-time winner Nikola Jokic, two-time Defensive Player of the Year Kawhi Leonard, and the youngest, Tyrese Maxey. This graph represents the number of wins each player adds to the team versus the amount of minutes they played during the 82-game season. The qualities of the Most Valuable player states the player must play at minimum 65 games and 20 minutes per game. In the top left of the graph, both Jokic and Gilgeous-Alexander are in the zone designated as the “most likely to be an MVP zone.” So, keep in mind our top candidates, one of whom should have been last year’s title holder.

Code 
ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(data=playerimpact, aes(x=playerseason, weight=bpm, fill = playerseason))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
  "darkgreen", #Giannis Antetokounmpo
  "red",  #Kawhi Leonard
  "purple",  #Nikola Jokić 2025
  "gold", #Nikola Jokić 
   "pink",  #Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 2025
  "orange",  #Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
  "royalblue",  #Stephen Curry
   "navy"  #Tyrese Maxey
  )) +
  labs(
    x="NBA MVP Canidates", 
    y="Box Plus Minus", 
    title="Which Players had the Most Influence during Games?", 
    subtitle="Our previous top contenders lead the way in these stats too.", 
    caption="Source: JR Rhodes-Winfrey"
    ) +
  theme_minimal()  +  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    ) +
  coord_flip()

Still, as we can see, both Gilgeous-Alexander and Jokic are striding hand in hand in leading the MVP race. In our box plus minus graph we see an upward trend between the two players however Jokic was still dominant in that phase of statting. Jokic lead in the box plus minus with a score of thirteen compared to Gilgeous-Alexander barely scraping over 10. It is getting pretty clear that whoever is going to be the MVP is going to be between the two, but the question is can Gilgeous-Alexander can get a convincing lead in the last graph to swing the MVP race.

Code 
Athletes <- c("Nikola Jokić", "Nikola Jokić 2025", "Shai Gilgeous-Alexander ", "Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 2025", "Giannis Antetokounmpo   ", "Stephen Curry", "Kawhi Leonard", "Tyrese Maxey")

impact|>  
filter(player_name %in% Athletes) |>
  select(player_name, season, rapm) |>
  arrange(desc(rapm)) |> 
  gt() |> 
  cols_label(
    rapm = "regularized adjusted plus minus") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Which Athletes Leaves their Team Stranded when Off the Court?",
    subtitle = "Number 15 dominates another column."
  ) |> tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "black", weight = "bold", align = "left"),
    locations = cells_title("title")
  ) |> tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "black", align = "left"),
    locations = cells_title("subtitle")
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = md("By: JR Rhodes-Winfrey")
  ) |>
  tab_style(
     locations = cells_column_labels(columns = everything()),
     style = list(
       cell_borders(sides = "bottom", weight = px(3)),
       cell_text(weight = "bold", size=12)
     )
   ) |>
  opt_row_striping() |> 
  opt_table_lines("none") |> 
   data_color(
    columns = rapm,
    method = "numeric",
    palette = c("red", "green"),
    domain = c(0, 6.5)
  )

As we can see here, last seasons MVP should have been Nikola Jokic as he has over performed his competition in the all three graphs. Surprisingly however, we do she a showing from Kawhi Leonard coming in second for the graph. Leading as number one in all three, he should have been the MVP compared to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. This would be Jokic’s fourth Most Valuable Player Award.
